scheme_evaluation.note: per-component scheme validated against THIS model's config at TP=4 x DP=1 BEFORE composing

components.name: attention
components.scheme: tensor-parallel by HEAD: q/k/v column-parallel (ShardTensorToMesh dim=-1 over a fused [q_d|k_d|v_d] layout), o_proj row-parallel (ShardTensorToMesh dim=0), closed by ttnn.experimental.all_reduce_async(cluster_axis=1, Sum)
constraints: GQA group must not straddle chips
components.check: 32 % 4 == 0 OK; 8 % 4 == 0 OK; group = 32/8 = 4, chip d owns q-heads [8d,8d+8) whose kv index [8d,8d+8)//4 == [2d,2d+2) == chip d's kv-heads OK

components.name: m_l_p
components.scheme: tensor-parallel on the INTERMEDIATE dim: gate/up column-parallel, down row-parallel, closed by all_reduce_async(cluster_axis=1, Sum)

components.name: decoder_layer
components.scheme: composite: replicated RMSNorms + sharded attention + sharded MLP; inherits attention's TP degree so both halves agree on the split; residual adds happen on replicated tensors after each all_reduce
constraints: both children agree on the same physical mesh axis
components.check: both children compute cluster_axis via the same helper -> axis 1 (the cols/TP axis of MeshShape(1,4)) OK

components.name: r_m_s_norm
components.scheme: REPLICATE (no shard dim exists: a width-shard would need an all_gather to compute the variance)
components.check: replication is the component's OWN graduated scheme, not a silent downgrade of a shardable one

components.name: rotary_embedding
components.scheme: REPLICATE (per-position lookup table; every chip rotates its own heads with the same angles)

pass_definition.gate_1: every routed graduated stub is still real ttnn; the three TP=4 bodies keep ShardTensorToMesh + all_reduce_async (NOT rewritten to replication). Asserted by scanning the live stub sources for a torch-compute fallback and by asserting the run recorded >0 ShardTensorToMesh weights and >0 collectives.
pass_definition.gate_2: all 5 graduated modules INVOKED inside the real forward path (recorded by tt/_invocation.py from inside each stub's forward, not by a coverage sweep); each one's output feeds downstream computation on the way to the emitted text.
pass_definition.gate_3: e2e PCC vs the HF golden >= 0.95, printed as `e2e PCC=<value>` on its own line immediately before the assert, on pass AND on fail. FINAL_PCC = min(prefill_parity, decode_parity), both injection-free: (a) prefill_parity = PCC of the TT prefill logits at EVERY real prompt position vs the HF forward (whole 32-layer stack, every graduated module, no decode); (b) decode_parity = PCC of the free-running per-step logits over the steps whose generated PREFIX both sides agree on.

validation_metric.why_not_plain_full-horizon_free-running_: greedy decoding is chaotic. Once the two sides pick differently at a near-tie the later steps are conditioned on DIFFERENT text, so their logits measure the tie-break, not the pipeline. Measured 2026-09-09 on 'List three interesting facts about the planet Jupiter.': identical for 13 tokens, then TT took 'Jupiter is the Largest...' and HF took 'Largest Planet...' where the GOLDEN's own top-2 logit gap was 0.196 -- a coin-flip. Full-horizon free-running PCC read 0.479 while prefill parity was 0.9986 and decode parity 0.9995. The comparable-step set is chosen by the DATA, never by hand, and the divergence step plus the golden's own top-2 gap there are always printed so a real error cannot hide behind 'it was just a tie'. A vacuous gate is blocked: the run fails if fewer than min(4, N) decode steps are comparable.
secondary: greedy token-id exact-match rate vs the golden ids
first divergence step + the golden's top-2 gap there
decoded text of both sides printed side by side
validation_metric.no_injection: no reference tensor or reference token is ever fed back into the TT chain; the TT side free-runs on its own output throughout

task_heads.behavioral_proof: the demo prints the prompt and the assistant text the TT pipeline generated; the test additionally prints the HF golden text so the two can be read side by side. Token-id match rate is reported.

decode_horizon.rule: STOP-TOKEN (priority 1): decode until the generated id is in generation_config.eos_token_id = [128001, 128008, 128009]; the SAME rule terminates the HF golden (generate() stops on the same ids).
decode_horizon.safety_cap: a max_new_tokens cap is ALWAYS applied and is passed identically to BOTH sides, so the two sequences are compared over the same, identically-terminated length. The on-device gate uses the small gate horizon GATE_MAX_NEW_TOKENS=40 to keep the device gate fast; the demo default is larger and settable via --max-new-tokens.
decode_horizon.never: the golden is never forced to a count the TT side invented; both get the same cap and the same eos set.

stub_routing.impl: HF AutoTokenizer (setup, outside the TT forward)
ttnn.embedding over a replicated embed_tokens weight (authored here; no graduated stub exists for it)
GRADUATED rotary_embedding -> TtLlamaRotaryEmbedding, called ONCE per forward, produces the (cos, sin) ttnn tensors consumed by every layer
GRADUATED decoder_layer -> TtLlamaDecoderLayer x 32, each internally invoking GRADUATED attention (TtLlamaAttention) and GRADUATED m_l_p (TtLlamaMLP)
GRADUATED r_m_s_norm -> TtLlamaRMSNorm on model.norm, feeding the lm_head
ttnn.linear over a replicated lm_head weight (authored here)
ttnn.argmax on device; the id feeds straight back into ttnn.embedding with no host round-trip

task_heads.kv_cache: resident per-layer K/V of shape [b, n_local_kv=2, C, 128] per chip; prefill writes it with ttnn.fill_cache, decode updates it with ttnn.experimental.paged_update_cache and reads it with ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention_decode. Decode NEVER recomputes the prefix.
adaptation_notes: attention._rot_tables currently accepts TORCH cos/sin. To feed it the GRADUATED rotary_embedding stub's ttnn output without a host round-trip, a ttnn branch is added (device-side reshape/repeat over the head axis) and the shape-keyed cache is bypassed for ttnn inputs (the tables change every decode step). The existing torch branch is left intact, so the per-component PCC tests keep passing.

attention gains an OPTIONAL kv-cache path (prefill fill / decode update+sdpa_decode). Both paths are pure ttnn and keep the same TP=4 sharding + all_reduce; the un-cached full-sequence causal path the component graduated on is unchanged.

orchestration.rationale: the checkpoint exposes exactly ONE task head with trained weights (LlamaForCausalLM), so there is one Call; it uses all 5 graduated modules, so by the shared-module rule it gets exactly one agent. Fanning out is also physically impossible here: all 4 chips are a single mesh that only one process can hold at a time.
orchestration.iteration: run on device with ./python_env/bin/python -m pytest <test> -s; fix wiring/stub and re-run until Gates 1-3 pass.

self_validation_plan: S1 - graduated inventory: re-derive the graduated set from bringup_status.json x _stubs/*.last_good_* at TEST TIME and assert the pipeline routed exactly that set (catches a stub that graduates later and gets left out).

S2 - Gate 1 nativeness: assert each routed stub module's source contains no torch-compute fallback in its forward, and that the three TP bodies still reference ShardTensorToMesh and all_reduce_async; assert the built pipeline actually created >0 sharded weights and >0 collectives at TP>1.

S3 - Gate 2 invocation: reset tt/_invocation.py's registry, run ONE real generation, assert the recorded set == the graduated set. Recording happens INSIDE each stub's forward, so it cannot be satisfied by a coverage sweep.
S4 - Gate 3 parity: PCC(TT step logits, HF step logits) >= 0.95, printed unconditionally before the assert.

S5 - no injected reference tensors: every stage consumes the previous TT stage's real output; the only HF tensors that enter are the tokenized input_ids and (for the golden helper) the reference itself.
S6 - demo/test share ONE pipeline: the test imports the same tt/pipeline.py function the demo calls; assert the demo module resolves to that same object.

S7 - stage trace contract (Command 3): trace_capture_selftest(device) captures and executes each stage in PIPELINE_STAGES host-op-free and PCC-checks the traced output against the eager reference, releasing each trace before the next.

S8 - host_op_selftest(): run the forward under scripts.tt_hw_planner.host_op_observer.observe_host_ops with tokenization and weight build OUTSIDE the observed region; assert verdict()['on_device'] is True.

pipeline_stages.derivation: architectures=[LlamaForCausalLM], is_encoder_decoder=false, no sub-configs, text output -> stages are [prefill, decode]
pipeline_stages.variable_dim: sequence axis; bound = max_position_embeddings (131072). Pinned to a fixed trace capacity C (default 512, shrunk and PRINTED if the trace region overflows).

trace_contract.prefill_trace_setup/prefill_trace_step/p: items = C (prefill retires C token positions per call)
trace_contract.decode_prefill/decode_step: decode_prefill seeds the resident self-attention KV; decode_step reads it and never recomputes the prefix
trace_contract.build_pipeline(device, model=None, layer: module-level factory that CONSTRUCTS AND RETURNS the resident pipeline object; layers=None means all 32; prefill and decode share the ONE decoder stack, so the per-stage overrides resolve to the same stack and must agree
trace_contract.stack_discovery: the 32 TtLlamaDecoderLayer objects are held as a plain Python list of one same-typed element type; the HF reference stays reachable on the object as .hf for ground-truth section structure

package_layout.tt/pipeline.py: the ONE shared chained forward (build_pipeline, PIPELINE_STAGES, run_text_generation, per-stage trace hooks, trace_capture_selftest, host_op_selftest)
